newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 31.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Yesterday, the German Federal parlaiment approved the Czech-German Declaration. Kohl took this opportunity to attempt to remedy his mistake which he made recently in Prague when he described property claims as open. During the vote, which was preceded by a three hour discussion, 578 out of 672 representatives voted for the declaration, and only 20 parliament members rejected it.

- Most of the coalition, but also social democratic representatives, yesterday appealed to Chairman of Parliament and the Social Democratic Party, Milos Zeman, to apologise to the public that his attempting to prove illegal cooperation between the Interior Ministry and the secret service (BIS) ended with a fiasco. Zeman did not comment on the request for an apology and refused to react to the results of the parliamentary committee for control of the BIS.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Aside from the increase in domestic postal tariffs which was already announced, international postal tariffs will increase on average by nearly six percent from April of this year.

- The chairman of the school workers union, Jaroslav Rossler, stated after a meeting of approximately one thousand teachers on a main square in Olomouc that the more politicians and the Education Minister refuse to resolve their problems, the more schools will enter into the strike.

- Transfering numerous clinics from General Faculty Hospital in Prague to the new Motol hospital is not, according to the Health Ministry, a decision solely for the directors of the hospital. The decision was made yesterday in a meeting with ministers Ivan Pilip and Jan Strasky and deputy vice-chancellor of Charles University and the dean of all Prague faculties, Pavel Klener.

PRAVO - A week ago, the cabinet approved the extension of securities amounting to 22.5 billion crowns to the Czech National Bank. The securities were issued because CNB goes through an international auditor and the auditor can look upon its debts to insolvent banks as unpayable and call for creating reserves which would equal the debts.
